title: Calibration artifact lifecycle: slicing, retention, and permissioning model
creator: Camila Ruiz
description: Goal: Design and ship an artifact lifecycle model for calibration runs (FP8/INT8 and associated metadata) in Redwood Console that supports sliced artifacts for targeted validation, clear TTL/retention policies, and RBAC-based permissions for access and deletion. The feature will enable reproducible accuracy validation, cheaper storage retention, and compliance-friendly audit trails. Scope covers UI/UX for run listing and artifact slicing controls, backend retention enforcement and garbage collection, per-artifact encryption and KMS metadata, and role-based access rules for view/download/delete operations.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-run artifact list with slices (e.g., 'full', 'task_A', 'edge-cases') and their size, accuracy delta, and created_at
Admins can configure default retention TTL at project level and override per-run; retention enforcement jobs garbage-collect expired artifacts and emit audit events
Permission matrix enforced: roles 'viewer', 'engineer', 'owner' map to read/download/run-reproduce, write-annotations, and delete artifacts respectively
Artifacts are versioned with a manifest (model hash, quant-profile id, seed, dataset-snapshot id) and are downloadable as signed bundles with provenance metadata
Calibration runs can produce sliced validation reports (per-slice accuracy metrics) and console can surface regression alerts based on configured thresholds
All artifact actions (create/download/delete/restore) are logged to audit stream with username, ip, and KMS key id when applicable

decisions: Artifact slicing will be producer-driven: calibration runner emits slice labels in manifest rather than Console auto-slicing
Default retention at project-level: 90 days. Per-run TTL allowed down to 7 days and up to 365 days. Admins can opt into indefinite retention with 'never_garbage_collect' flag
Soft-delete window of 14 days before permanent deletion to support restores and legal holds
Use signed tar.gz bundles containing manifest.json, metrics.csv, and artifact blobs for reproducibility and offline validation
risks: Large storage costs if users opt for indefinite retention; mitigated by default 90-day TTL and quota warnings
Accidental deletion by high-privilege roles; mitigated by soft-delete, confirmation UX, and audit trails
Manifest schema changes may break older run reproduction; will version manifests and include compatibility layer
